Jamie — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and an ask to lock down the numbers so we can put together a concrete hosted pricing sketch.

Call recap (short):
- BrightLoop product: user-facing summarization and chat in the mobile app (customer support + proactive tips).
- Primary latency SLO: 150–200ms p95 for short chat prompts; spikes to 400–500ms acceptable during rare peak windows.
- Data residency: US only (no EU data flows).

Numbers I have from the call (please confirm):
1) Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~120M tokens/month (user messages + model responses combined).
2) Peak TPS: 55 concurrent token-generation TPS at 99th percentile during promotional spikes (estimated 6–8 hour window).
3) Typical request shape: 1.2k requests/sec at peak, average prompt length ~120 tokens, average completion ~80 tokens (total ~200 tokens/request).

Ask: can you confirm the monthly token number (120M) and peak TPS estimate (55)? If those look right, we’ll produce two hosted pricing options: a conservative commit with burst buffer and a pay-as-you-go path with rate-limited guards.

Attached: blank ratecard + example traffic CSV for your review (I populated traffic shape using the numbers above).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the numbers or send corrected CSV by EOD Wed 9/15.
- We’ll send an initial pricing sketch and unit economic breakdown ($/1M tokens) and expected monthly invoice ranges by Thu 9/16.

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks Karthik — good summary, pretty close to what we discussed. A couple of corrections / clarifications:
- Monthly tokens: our internal dashboards show ~95–130M tokens depending on retention of conversation context; 120M is a reasonable median to price off.
- Peak TPS: the 55 TPS you noted is tokens/sec; confirm you meant token TPS (not requests/sec). We see peaks of ~40 requests/sec during promo, which at ~200 tokens/request => ~8k tokens/sec. That would be 8k token/sec peak, which is much higher than 55 — I think you meant 55 requests/sec or 55 RPS.

To be explicit:
- Median monthly tokens: 120M
- Peak requests/sec (RPS): ~55 RPS during promos (6–8 hr windows)
- Peak tokens/sec (token TPS): ~11k token/sec at very worst-case (we rarely hit this, maybe for a few 15–30 minute bursts)

I attached a .csv export from our analytics for Aug which shows minute-level spikes. Procurement looped in — they’ll want to see expected invoice ranges and a simple SLA statement.

—Jamie

Jamie — thanks for the CSV. Two quick clarifying points from an econ perspective before we put numbers in HubSpot:
1) For hosted pricing we price primarily per-token for generation and per-embedding where applicable. For estimation here we’ll treat all activity as generation tokens. If you have embedding usage separately let us know.
2) You mentioned occasional 15–30 minute token bursts to ~11k token/sec. For capacity planning we model the 99th token TPS over a rolling 5–minute window. Can you confirm whether the 11k number is sustained for 1 minute or fluctuates a lot (e.g., high for 10–20 seconds then back down)? 5-minute sustained vs short microbursts materially impacts reserve capacity and unit price.

Pricing sketch (very preliminary):
- Pay-as-you-go: $28 / 1M tokens (no commit, immediate availability, standard rate limits and soft-burst throttling).
- Committed monthly slab (120M median): tiered unit price to $20 — $18 / 1M tokens depending on term & 12-month commit; includes a 2x short-burst buffer and access to burst pool for paid overages.
- Dedicated/reserved: invite-only quote for >1B tokens/mo or strict latency/99th SLOs.

We’ll produce a formal one-pager comparing the two paths with expected invoice ranges based on 95M / 120M / 130M scenarios and include an estimate for peak exposure (how much burst buffer we’d need to keep under your latency SLO).

Can you answer the 5-minute vs microburst question? Also confirm if BrightLoop plans to keep conversation context windows across sessions (that increases per-session token counts).

Thanks — Marissa
